1 
Project: Federico-Tena World Population Historical Database 
Web site: https://www.uc3m.es/investigacion/federico-tena-population 
Description of the project:  Project developed by  Giovanni Federico (New Y ork 
University Abu Dhabi) and Antonio Tena-Junguito (Universidad Carlos III de Madrid). 
We have estimated yearly series of total population for all polities (colonies and 
independent countries) from 1800 to 1938. Overall, the data -base features 174 series 
for a total of 21815 country -year observations. We have relied mainly on work by 
historical demographers, who have painstakingly collected, assessed and, when 
necessary, corrected official data and any available information. We have filled gaps 
with interpolations and have extrapolated backward the population from the earliest 
available figure to 1800 or forward from the latest one to 1938. We have taken also 
into account the population movements in neighboring or otherwise comparable 
polities and also the available information on demographic crises (most notably the 
Spanish flu). The country data refer to present (de facto) population when possible, 
adjusted to mid-year.

D
ataset content: Our new estimate of world population by countries are annual series 
ranging from 1800 to 1938. We organize the data set by continent and single excel (and 
txt) files by polities (that is more specific than countries) in thousand people (000). 
Methodology and Sources: We have estimated population for a total of 21815 
polity/year observations for 174 polities at their historical borders between 1800 and 
1838. We detail the sources and methods of estimation and criteria used in: Federico, 
Giovanni; Tena- Junguito, Antonio (2023): How many people on earth? World 
2 
population 1800-1938. Working Papers in Economic History 23-02/ Instituto Figuerola 
Universidad Carlos III de Madrid. URI: http://hdl.handle.net/10016/36431 
Time series coverage. In general terms, the data cover the period 1800 -1938. They all 
include natives, as their omission would bias upward the growth of population and 
refer to current borders – so that some series cover only part of the period (e.g. Austria-
Hungary stops in 1918, Czechoslovakia, Hungary and Poland start in 1919). 
Geographical coverage: The minimal geographical units are the countries, when they 
have political independence, otherwise they are mentioned by the current name used 
by metropolitan political imperial or colonial administrative political units. The number 
of polities varies only as a consequence of changes in political boundaries.  
File c ontent: Wo rld file includes c ontinents or p olities units i n E xcel fi les r anked in 
alphabetical order according to current borders and historical names.
